question: I need help with setting up two different emails on my website. One for receiving order invoices and the other for general inquiries. Im specifically looking for guidance on how to set the email address for order confirmations in the Business Info section of my sites settings.
candidate_answer:
To set up two different emails on your website—one for order invoices and another for general inquiries—follow these steps:

- Purchase additional business email addresses if not already done.
- Create the specific emails, e.g., orders@yourdomain.com for order invoices and info@yourdomain.com for general inquiries.
- In your account, go to Business Email.
- Click "Show User Info" on the relevant account.
- Click the "More Actions" icon next to the account you want to set up.
- Select "Set Up User" and sign in to your Google Workspace account.
- To set the email address for order confirmations specifically in the Business Info section of your site settings, assign the orders@yourdomain.com email there to ensure order-related communications are directed correctly.

This process allows you to manage incoming emails by department effectively [S1].

question: I need to update the og:image for my entire site to ensure the correct image appears when the link is posted on social media. I also want to know if this will affect the image when the link is posted in an email or on Instagram.
candidate_answer:
To update the og:image for your entire site:

- Go to your site's settings in the Wix Editor.
- Click on Website settings.
- Scroll down to General social image and click Upload Image.
- Select or upload the desired image.
- Click Choose File, then Save at the top of the dashboard.
- Publish your site to apply changes [S1].

Regarding the impact on other platforms:

- The og:image primarily controls the image shown when your site link is shared on social media platforms.
- For emails, the image display depends on the email client and how it handles link previews; og:image may or may not be used.
- Instagram does not generate link previews with og:image when posting links, so the image may not appear there.

Thus, updating the og:image ensures consistent branding on social media shares but may not affect email or Instagram link previews significantly.

[S1]

question: Im unable to access the Google Maps element in the footer of my Wix site. Im having trouble removing it, and I dont know where the overlapping items feature is located.
candidate_answer:
To access and remove the Google Maps element in the footer of your Wix site when it's difficult to select:

- Use the **Layers panel** to locate the Google Maps element in the footer:
  - Open your Wix Editor.
  - Click the **Layers icon** at the bottom of the editor.
  - Select **Footer** to see all elements in the footer.
  - Find and select the Google Maps element from the list.

- Use the **Overlapping Items feature** to select the element if it is behind another:
  - Right-click on the element that is covering the Google Maps element.
  - Hover over **Overlapping Items** in the context menu.
  - Select the Google Maps element from the list to access it.

This will allow you to select and remove the Google Maps element even if it is overlapped or hidden behind other elements [S1].
